intended_object: The Selmer structure (in the sense of Mazur–Rubin) on the Galois module E(Kˢ)[m] whose Selmer group is the m-Selmer group. It uses restriction to each G_{L_i}, induced by the embeddings τ_i, as localisation, and takes as local condition at L_i the kernel of H¹(G_{L_i}, E[m]) → H¹(G_{L_i}, E), i.e. the image of the local Kummer map. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Silverman X.4.
explanation:
The library's `SelmerStructure` bundles four pieces of data for each index i: a continuous group map H_i → G, an equivariant map M → N_i, a continuity condition, and a local-condition subgroup of H¹(H_i, N_i). Its Selmer group is the set of classes whose localisation lies in every local condition.

This definition fills these in as follows:
- the group maps are G_{L_i} → G_K, induced by τ_i : Kˢ → L_iˢ;
- the coefficient maps are base change E(Kˢ)[m] → E(L_iˢ)[m];
- the local condition is the kernel of the map H¹(G_{L_i}, E[m]) → H¹(G_{L_i}, E) induced by the inclusion E[m] ⊂ E.

This matches Silverman X.4, where Sel_m = ker(H¹(G_K, E[m]) → ∏_v H¹(G_v, E)). The library proves `mem_selmerGroup_iff`, which says membership is the same as the image in H¹(G_K, E) lying in Sha. When E is elliptic and m is invertible in K, the local condition equals the image of the local Kummer map, by local exactness (`mem_selmerGroup_iff_forall_torsionRes_mem_range_kummerMap`).

The setting is already general: any field K, any family of extensions with embeddings, and any m. Working over Kˢ rather than K̄ is standard Galois cohomology and agrees with the usual definition when m is invertible. The kernel form needs no hypotheses, as the module documentation states.

Mathlib has no Selmer groups or Selmer structures for elliptic curves, so there is no counterpart.
